narrative.overview: The interface is a chronicler's ledger suspended in deep space. Near-black surfaces hold ice entries; every number is a witness, every panel a page of the chronicle. The living map below — green pasture, forest, slate water, amber and teal territories — is the world that burns and rebuilds inside the void; the HUD is the archive that records its causes and effects without ever shouting over it. The archive is void-bound and ledger-calm: a near-black space field, body text in star-white, secondary text in space dust, and a single cold ice used with the discipline of a seal. Surfaces are flattened: panels go solid and opaque, retiring translucent glass and backdrop blur; depth comes from tonal separation against the void rather than translucency. Components are refined and restrained — quiet, precise, instrumental — with small uppercase letterspaced labels, monospaced figures, hairline borders, and minimal motion.
keyCharacteristics: Void-bound: near-black space field, star-white text, ice seal
Ledger-calm: uppercase micro-labels and tabular mono figures on every data surface
Restrained instrumentality: hairline borders, small radii, no decoration
The map leads: instruments sit at the edges and recede in hierarchy
Space-derived: the void and the star-white seal are the palette core

rules.name: The Ice Seal Rule
rules.body: Ice covers ≤10% of any surface. It appears where the player acts or where truth is stamped: the active speed, the hash, the carry. When ice appears twice, the screen is wrong.

rules.name: The Two-People Rule
rules.body: Hearth Amber and Iron Tide appear only where faction meaning is at stake — ownership, control, allegiance. Never as decoration.

rules.name: The Brand Mark Rule
rules.body: The logo is the title. Where the brand mark appears, never re-type the name beside or above it — the mark carries the wordmark. On the landing page the cover is the mark itself, sitting directly on the field with no frame and no tag.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: Every figure is monospaced with tabular numerals; a number never wraps, breaks, or loses alignment with its column label.

rules.name: The Label Voice Rule
rules.body: Micro-labels are always uppercase and letterspaced; sentence case is reserved for descriptive body text only.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are solid. No backdrop-filter, no translucent fills; separation comes from tone and the hairline, never from blur.

rules.name: The Deep Field Rule
rules.body: Atmosphere is background paint, never surface. The vignette, the ruled frame, the nebula, and the star scatter sit behind the content, stay still under reduced motion, and never compete with the map or the instruments.

dos: Do keep Ice rare — active state, the hash, the carry; one ice moment per surface.
Do set every figure in mono with tabular numerals under its uppercase micro-label.
Do use Hearth Amber and Iron Tide only for faction meaning.
Do flatten surfaces: solid opaque panels, tone + hairline for separation.
Do preserve the map's readability — instruments at the edges, map centered and unobstructed.
Do keep the brand mark (public/logo.png) on the space field — it is the palette's source and the title, never recolored and never re-typed (The Brand Mark Rule).
donts: Don't drift into a colorful cartoon strategy palette — no saturated multicolor UI.
Don't drift into a sterile SaaS dashboard — no blue links, dense tables, or empty-state illustrations.
Don't drift into a military-green tactical console — no olive/khaki, no angular HUD clutter.
Don't add translucency or backdrop blur; the glass look is being retired.
Don't add a second display face — Cinzel is the system's single engraved voice, and the HUD stays sans.
Don't add saturation beyond the three accents (ice, amber, teal) and the terrain gamut.
Don't recolor, tint, or distort the brand mark — it is the palette's source of truth.
Don't re-type the title where the brand mark carries it — no text wordmark beside the logo, and no cover title above it.
